title: Gated kernel scheduler for attention fanout reduction and decode-pipeline pacing
creator: Priya Nair
description: Introduce a gated kernel scheduling layer that reduces attention kernel fanout during prefill and applies pacing to the decode pipeline. The gate performs lightweight micro-probing to choose between FlashAttention v2/v3 fast paths and a conservative baseline kernel to contain regressions observed in high-concurrency tails. Goals: reduce 95/99th latency on multi-tenant hosts, limit memory fragmentation when switching kernels, and provide safe automatic fallback for problematic sequence-length / batch-size combinations.
description_long: Problem: Recent canaries showed sporadic 99th-percentile latency spikes on Dedicated nodes when FlashAttention v3 kernels were aggressively selected for wide batch-prefill workloads. Root cause hypotheses include kernel memory allocator contention and an unexpected working-set growth during v3 tiling for middling sequence lengths. Proposed solution: implement a gated scheduler that probes small representative batches to estimate per-request kernel latency and memory delta, then selects a kernel variant. During prefill, the gate will limit fanout by queuing/merging requests that would trigger high memory churn. During decode, the gate injects lightweight pacing (milliseconds) when kernel-switching is frequent to avoid thrashing.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Gate performs micro-probe < 3ms added overhead for >95% requests. 2) 99th latency reduced by >= 15% on regression workloads in benchmark cluster. 3) Automatic fallback engages without data loss and is observable in Console. 4) No increase in error-rate or token corruption. 5) Feature gated behind runtime flag and canary rollout path documented.
technical_notes: Micro-probing: run 3 short warmup runs on candidate kernels (v2/v3/baseline) using representative batch sizes; aggregate median latency and resident memory delta.
Telemetry: emit 'kernel.probe.latency_ms', 'kernel.probe.mem_delta_bytes', 'kernel.selection.reason', and 'gate.pacing_ms' to attributes.trace and Console metrics.
Fallback policy: if probe shows >20% mem_delta or observed tail latency > SLO_threshold * 1.5, select baseline; record selection in request metadata for traceability.
Prefill fanout reduction: limit concurrent prefill streams per-GPU to configured soft limit (default 6) and queue extra requests with priority decay to preserve latency SLOs.
Decode pacing: when kernel-switch frequency detected > 5 switches/min for a session, insert 2-10ms pacing between tokens to stabilize allocator behavior.
Compatibility: support both FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels; add detection for driver/kernel features that make v3 unsafe (e.g., known buggy cu* versions).
Memory safety: add guard to abort v3 path if observed working set exceeds 90% of available device memory minus reserved runtime footprint.
Bench harness: extend existing perf-runner to sweep batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16,32] and seq-len [64,128,256,512,1024] across kernel variants and record breakdowns.

canary_plan: Stage 0: opt-in on internal perf cluster (small subset). Stage 1: 5% traffic on dedicated canary machines for non-critical customers. Stage 2: Ramp to 30% with detailed tracing. Rollback if 99th latency increases >5% or error-rate increases >0.1%.
final_notes: This ticket is implementing a safety-first performance enhancement rather than an aggressive optimizer. Prioritize observability and rollback mechanics over maximal throughput gains in alpha. Expect follow-ups to expose heuristics tuning and to upstream any allocator fixes to FlashAttention if root cause confirmed.
